info.name: Order Fulfillment System (MongoDB)
info.description:
End-to-end test cases for examples/order-system-mongodb.

API contract is identical to order-system (Postgres): same URL paths, same request shapes,
same response shapes. The SQL postman collection can be reused against this implementation
after changing the environment variables (ports are the same by default).

SETUP
1. Start infrastructure: MongoDB, Redis, Kafka
2. Start all four apps with DEMO_MODE=true:
     DEMO_MODE=true java -jar order-external-mock/target/*.jar
     java -jar order-manager/target/*.jar
     java -jar order-steward/target/*.jar
     java -jar order-acknowledge/target/*.jar

Folders 01-05 and 08 need DEMO_MODE=true.
Folders 06, 07 work either way.

Kafka propagation is not instant:
  newman run order-system-mongodb.postman_collection.json --delay-request 4000

item.name: 01. Happy Path
item.description: The full lifecycle, one step at a time. Requires DEMO_MODE=true so nothing advances on its own.

request.description:
The real ingress: an external party publishes the order onto Kafka. The manager consumes it into the order-intake-event flow.

The fulfillment_id is generated server-side — just like order-system (Postgres).
Drains the manager outbox to Kafka. In DEMO_MODE the scheduler does nothing, so this is what moves the order to the steward.
The Kafka ingress does not answer with a fulfillment id (nobody is waiting), so it is read back from the manager and stored for the SoR steps below.

exec: pm.test("order is in the read model", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: Ticks every SCHEDULED fulfillment. Resumes the graph past checkpoint 1: SCHEDULED -> DISPATCHED.
Drains the steward outbox: sor.dispatch and every fulfillment.status event.
Publishes the 'validated' milestone on its SoR topic.

exec: pm.test("published to the SoR topic", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("published to the SoR topic", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("published to the SoR topic", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: Drains the steward outbox: the SETTLED fulfillment.status event.
Publishes the external order-status notification staged in the manager's outbox.
The external report, served from the manager's read model.

item.name: 02. SoR Failure - at Validation
item.description: The SoR reports failure at 'validated'. The fulfillment ends FAILED with reason sor_validated.

exec: pm.test("order is in the read model", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("published to the SoR topic", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: 03. SoR Failure - at Preprocess
item.description: The SoR reports failure at 'preprocessed'. The fulfillment ends FAILED with reason sor_preprocessed.

exec: pm.test("order is in the read model", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("published to the SoR topic", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("published to the SoR topic", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: 04. SoR Failure - at Process
item.description: The SoR reports failure at 'processed'. The fulfillment ends FAILED with reason sor_processed.

exec: pm.test("order is in the read model", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("published to the SoR topic", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: 05. Business Rejection (amount = 0)
item.description: An order that fails the graph's own validation never reaches the SoR. The lifecycle stops at REJECTED after two transitions and no sor.dispatch is ever published.

request.description: The rejection happens inside the steward's graph, so its fulfillment.status event must be relayed before the manager can know about it. Without this step the manager still reports RECEIVED.

item.name: 06. Intake Validation (REST)
item.description: The REST ingress answers a bad order with 400 through the flow's exception handler. These run with or without DEMO_MODE.

exec: pm.test("message names the problem", () => pm.expect(b.message).to.include("Missing order_id"));
pm.test("message names the problem", () => pm.expect(b.message).to.include("Missing route"));
pm.test("message names the problem", () => pm.expect(b.message).to.include("Missing payload"));

item.name: 07. Kafka Ingress + Dead Letter
item.description: Over Kafka nobody is waiting for an answer, so a malformed order must dead-letter rather than be silently dropped.

exec: pm.test("found in the read model", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: 4. Malformed order via Kafka  (bad order_id prefix)

request.description: The mock performs no validation — sending a bad order is the point.

exec: pm.test("the mock publishes it regardless", () => pm.response.to.have.status(202));

request.description: It should be sitting in orders.inbound.dlq instead.

item.name: 08. Idempotency
item.description: Self-contained: runs a full lifecycle, then replays all three milestones against the settled fulfillment. Each replay finds the Redis record already consumed, so the graph skips and the read model stays unchanged. Needs DEMO_MODE=true.

exec: pm.test("order is in the read model", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("published to the SoR topic", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("published to the SoR topic", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("published to the SoR topic", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: 12. Replay: SoR Validated  (pass) — should be no-op
13. Replay: SoR Preprocessed  (fail) — should be no-op
14. Final Steward Relay  (should have nothing to relay)
